rows.estimation_basis: Estimates are grounded in reference project 004-healthcare-patient-app (Patient Appointment and Telehealth App: 3,900 hours, 22 weeks). We matched the core modules directly: Patient Flutter app (~850h vs reference 900h), appointment scheduling (~480h vs reference 520h), video consultations (~380h vs reference 380h), secure messaging and reminders (~420h vs reference 420h), counsellor web dashboard (~550h vs reference 560h), HIPAA security/audit (~310h vs reference 300h), and QA/store submission (~360h vs reference 340h). The external HL7 FHIR EHR integration from the reference (480h) was excluded as the client brief does not require external hospital EHR connectivity, resulting in a pragmatic baseline of ~3,260 to 3,940 total delivery hours.

Estimates are strictly benchmarked against reference project 'Learning Management System for Corporate Training' (id=007-edtech-lms, 2,800 total hours across 18 weeks). The reference breakdown was reused across matching modules: User/Shift Management (200-240h vs ref 220h), Course Authoring (440-500h vs ref 480h), Video Delivery (280-320h vs ref 300h), Quizzes with Attempt Limits (320-360h vs ref 340h), Certificates & Validity (340-380h vs ref 360h), SCORM Ingestion & Runtime (400-460h vs ref 420h), and Shift Reporting (260-300h vs ref 280h). DevOps and QA work (totaling 400-460h) aligns with the reference project's 400h allocation for delivery, testing, and stabilization.

Estimates are directly benchmarked against Reference Project 008-mobile-field-service (Offline-First Field Service App for Technicians, 3,600 total delivery hours across 21 weeks). Scope requirements for the pest control application match the reference architecture closely: offline local persistence with SQLite (720-800h vs. 760h reference), mobile inspection and job forms (490-550h vs. 520h reference), photo/signature capture and resilient queueing (280-330h vs. 300h reference), back-office scheduling console (600-680h vs. 640h reference), and ERP integration for jobs and invoices (480-560h vs. 520h reference). Lessons learned from Reference 008 emphasizing sync edge cases, device fragmentation, and dedicated field validation have been incorporated into explicit allocations for QA, device testing, and the stabilization pilot (380-440h).

Estimates are directly benchmarked against reference project 'Fleet Tracking Portal for a Logistics Operator' (id=001-logistics-fleet-portal, 3000 total hours, 20 weeks). For this engagement, module hours were adapted to reflect 2 telematics suppliers instead of 3 (supplier integration calibrated from 520h down to 360-440h), and a focused fleet size of 250 school buses operating primarily during split morning/afternoon shifts. Live map tracking (360-440h) and alerts engine (340-420h) closely mirror the reference modules given identical real-time WebSocket, spatial geofence, and idle detection complexities. Driver/vehicle management (200-260h) and reporting (280-340h) were adjusted for school route assignment and daily per-route run summaries. QA, DevOps, and UAT (totaling 700-900h combined) maintain the historical ratio necessary for mission-critical transportation safety.

Estimates are grounded in historical metrics from reference project 003-ecommerce-b2b-marketplace (B2B Marketplace for Industrial Parts, total 6,100 hours across 30 weeks). Analogue modules were adjusted to match classic car auction domain specifics: The catalogue import pipeline (620h historically) maps to the Vehicle Inventory Ingestion & Mapping Engine (580-660h); search and faceted filtering on Elasticsearch (540h historically) maps to the Faceted Vehicle Search & Follow Engine (500-580h); Stripe Connect split payments (700h historically) informs the Deposit Holds & Split Settlements module (640-740h); and the Supplier portal (820h historically) is adapted into the Dealer Management Console (520-620h), trimmed of industrial quote workflows. Specific scope additions without a direct 1:1 match in reference 003 include the dedicated Real-Time Bidding & Anti-Sniping Engine (680-800h), which replaces standard cart/checkout flows with distributed WebSocket bidding and atomic Redis state management. QA, DevOps, and admin back-office hours closely align with the reference project's actual distribution to guarantee resilient, production-ready delivery.

Estimates were calibrated against two historical reference projects: 'KYC Onboarding Platform for a Digital Bank' (id=002-fintech-kyc-onboarding, 5,200 total hours) and 'B2B Marketplace for Industrial Parts' (id=003-ecommerce-b2b-marketplace, 6,100 total hours). The verification wizard, external identity integration, compliance console, and PII encryption scope were mapped directly from the KYC Onboarding benchmark (which allocated 480h, 460h, 720h, and 420h respectively). We adjusted the compliance review scope slightly downward (580-680h) as the gig platform requires standard right-to-work and background screening rather than full banking PEP/sanctions and regulatory reporting. The marketplace and payout modules were baselined against the B2B Marketplace project, drawing from its catalog/search filtering (540h), Stripe Connect split payments (700h), and admin moderation workflows (520h). Cross-cutting infrastructure, DevOps, and comprehensive QA/security testing are sized based on the actual delivery ratios observed across both reference benchmarks.

Estimates are directly grounded in past delivery metrics from two analogous reference projects: '006-saas-analytics-dashboard' and '001-logistics-fleet-portal'. From Reference 006, we reused the effort benchmarks for high-volume Kafka ingestion (520h baseline vs. 480-560h planned), ClickHouse analytical modeling and tenant query APIs (1,200h combined baseline vs. 580-680h planned), the customisable Angular drag-and-drop dashboard builder (1,000h baseline vs. 850-1,050h planned), and the scheduled PDF/email reporting service (380h baseline vs. 320-400h planned). From Reference 001, we adapted the multi-tenant RBAC module (160h baseline vs. 160-200h planned), the device/installer CRUD provisioning portal modeled after driver/vehicle fleet management (240h baseline vs. 240-300h planned), and the real-time threshold alert engine modeled after route deviation alerts (380h baseline vs. 340-420h planned). Infrastructure, QA, and load testing are budgeted at enterprise scale (~1,130-1,360h combined) reflecting the historical post-release stabilisation, performance testing, and multi-tenant isolation validation observed across both reference deliveries.

Estimates were synthesized from two relevant historical reference projects: 'Offline-First Field Service App for Technicians' (008-mobile-field-service) and 'Internal HR Knowledge Assistant (RAG)' (005-hr-internal-ai-assistant). For the offline data architecture and synchronization, we referenced the 760h baseline from 008, scoped to ~600-750h reflecting document caching and visit queues without complex multi-party checklist merges. The CRM integration (360-460h) was modeled against the ERP integration (520h) from 008, adapted for Salesforce REST/Composite APIs. For the RAG pipeline, document ingestion, retrieval, streaming chat UI, and evaluation harness, estimates were adapted directly from 005 (totaling ~1,000h for core AI modules), with additional hours allocated for page-level citation extraction and pharmaceutical regulatory compliance guardrails. QA, pilot validation, and mobile DevOps release reflect the 660h combined baseline from 008 adjusted for healthcare field testing.

Estimates are grounded in historical metrics from reference project 'Patient Appointment and Telehealth App' (id=004-healthcare-patient-app, 3,900 hours, 22 weeks). Analogous components were mapped directly: the Flutter mobile app baseline was preserved (~850-980h vs reference 900h), appointment scheduling and conflict handling (~480-560h vs reference 520h), Twilio video consultation (~360-440h vs reference 380h), notifications (~280-340h vs reference 420h, adjusted down as SMS/EHR prescription alerts are reduced to coaching reminders), and QA/store submission (~340-420h vs reference 340h). The EHR/FHIR integration from the reference was removed and replaced with new modules tailored to this brief: Apple HealthKit / Google Health Connect integration (450-550h), dynamic leaderboard calculations (300-380h), and an HR participation portal (400-480h). Total effort spans 4,180 to 5,070 human engineering hours over 24 weeks.

No historical reference projects were provided for this brief. The estimate has been constructed completely bottom-up based on standard enterprise engineering metrics and historical experience with comparable warehouse inventory management systems. Effort allocations include holistic team delivery responsibilities: architecture design, backend and PWA development, scanner input normalization, variance calculation engines, QA verification with physical hardware emulation, DevOps deployment, and post-launch stabilization.

No reference projects were provided for this proposal. The estimates have been constructed bottom-up based on general enterprise mobile engineering experience, accounting for full lifecycle delivery including discovery, UX/UI, frontend mobile implementation, backend APIs, automated CI/CD with Fastlane, comprehensive QA/UAT testing across native platforms, and store submissions. Because no direct empirical reference data was available, a variance margin of approximately 35% is factored between minimum and maximum hours.

No reference projects were provided for this engagement; therefore, the estimate is built bottom-up from general engineering experience across custom scheduling applications, role-based workflows, and algorithmic rule engines. Scope accounts for full delivery lifecycle overhead including discovery, UX, testing, deployment, and stabilization.

Effort is calculated bottom-up across full software lifecycle activities, including discovery, UI/UX, double-entry financial-grade ledger implementation, gift card provider integration with async retry policies, comprehensive QA/UAT cycles, automated CI/CD infrastructure, and stabilization. A moderate uncertainty buffer of approximately 25-30% is incorporated within the hours range to account for third-party provider API contracting and sandbox nuances.
